answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut mandate combined with 94% line utilization creates acute cost pressure without switching risk tolerance. Memory_c6 demonstrates that multi-year commitments with the incumbent unlock volume pricing—critical leverage for aggressive negotiation. Memory_c2 shows that switching vendors can cut unit costs sharply, which gives us a credible outside option to use in renegotiation. The 14-day deadline rules out full vendor evaluation but allows aggressive negotiation with incumbent while preserving the option to switch if terms don't move. This approach leverages memory_c4 (benchmarking recovers margin) without memory_c1's lock-in risk or memory_c3's complexity of adding a second source under time pressure. Negotiation targets both price and terms to hit the 18% target while keeping integration stable through the 94% utilization window. If negotiation fails, we have 1-2 days to execute a switch to the low-cost vendor or defer on month-to-month (memory_c5 pattern). This preserves decision optionality and avoids single-decision lock-in given the constraints.
